title: Page order: match the arrival, answer questions in order, one dominant risk
decision_task: How to order a landing or home page: the opening matches awareness and the inbound message; the body follows the prospect's own question sequence; button copy depends on readiness. / Which risk reducer an offer, page or email uses: diagnose the single biggest perceived risk and match the reducer to it, instead of defaulting to a guarantee or testimonials.
applies_when: Any landing, home or service page
Rewrite of a page that repeats proof or risk reducers in random places
Offer pages, booking pages, trial sign-ups, checkout-adjacent copy
exclusions: Most-aware traffic on a short offer page, where the sequence collapses to offer, terms, CTA
Pages whose order is fixed by platform (marketplace listings)
Free, low-commitment actions where extra reassurance adds clutter
No VOC or owner input to tell which risk dominates (then ask the owner a single question)
required_inputs: Stated arrival mindset, desired action and the belief change needed between them
Owner-confirmed list of existing risk reducers
evidence_requirements: Coded hesitations or objections with counts (voc-research)
Confirmed reducers the business actually offers (trial, guarantee, demo, insurance, named reviews)
missing_data_behavior: No VOC to tell which risk dominates: ask the owner one question; label it owner judgement.
Reducer not offered by the business (e.g. a guarantee): owner note only, never in copy.
alternatives_when_constrained: No reviews: the 'people like them' step uses a mechanism, process photos or confirmed counts, never placeholders
No customers yet: skip peer proof; strengthen mechanism and risk reversal
Low traffic: no A/B test; ship the ordered version and track the end conversion over time
No reviews: use owner's top three hesitations heard in sales calls, labelled owner-reported
No customers yet: rely on mechanism and reversible first step
Low traffic: pick one reducer and track booking or purchase rate over time rather than A/B testing

decision_branches.if: Most-aware traffic on a short offer

decision_branches.then: Follow the prospect's question order; each proof once.

decision_branches.if: Dominant risk is will-it-work / worth-it / approval
decision_branches.then: Demo / guarantee + same-type proof / named peers, near the CTA.

implementation_steps: Write three lines: arrival mindset, desired action, belief change needed
Opening (roughly the first screen): message match to the ad or email plus awareness-appropriate framing
Body: what this is → why it matters to this reader → people like them use it → how it works → what changes for them → why believe it → next step; skip or merge steps the reader does not need
Place each proof once, where its question is asked; do not repeat social proof and guarantees at random points
Readiness-based buttons: early buttons state the benefit of continuing; final buttons state the step
Judge any test on the end conversion (booking, purchase), not clicks, especially when button count changes
Rate decision risk for one reader: low, medium, high
Classify hesitations into: will it work, is it worth it, will it fit my life, will others approve, will I be satisfied
Pick the top risk by VOC count (or owner judgement, labelled)
Match the reducer: demo or mechanism for will-it-work; guarantee, price clarity or trial for worth-it; setup help or flexible terms for fit; peer proof from the same segment for approval
Place it at or just above the primary CTA; consider removing copy that raises new doubts
Any reducer the business does not offer goes to the owner as a suggestion, never into copy
metrics: End conversion rate by traffic source
Scroll depth to the CTA section
Ratio of clicks to conversions (to catch click-inflating buttons)
Conversion at the step where the reducer sits
Pre-purchase questions received on the topic
guardrails: Every proof item traces to confirmed facts (lint.ts claim ledger)
No authority proof that is not confirmed and permitted
The question sequence is a scaffold; do not print its labels as headings verbatim
Never invent a guarantee, trial, user count or peer logo
Peer counts (e.g. 'N businesses this week') only from confirmed, current data
One reducer focus per page, not all five risk types
observation_window: 2 to 4 weeks or a pre-set number of end conversions per variant before judging. / 2 to 4 weeks or a pre-set conversion count.
stop_conditions: Clicks rise but end conversions do not: revert button changes
Bounce rate on mobile rises after the rewrite: review the opening match
Owner cannot confirm the reducer: drop it from copy
Conversion falls after adding reducer copy: review whether it surfaced a new doubt
review_triggers: Owner corrects an input this playbook relies on
A metric or guardrail crosses its bound
The underlying source or platform rule changes
climbos_location: skills/landing-pages/SKILL.md steps 3 to 5 (hero, section order, proof placement) and the page brief format / skills/landing-pages/SKILL.md step 6 (objection mapping) and step 3 (micro-copy under CTA); skills/voc-research/SKILL.md step 8 (counter types)

interpretation: LABELLED INTERPRETATION: the 108% case is a bundled change with no reported statistics, so it shows the approach can coincide with large gains, not that it causes them. The durable parts are the ordering logic and judging on end conversions.
LABELLED INTERPRETATION: ClimbOS maps counters by JTBD force (anxiety, habit, price). The risk-type lens is finer-grained for anxiety, and it adds 'pick one'. They are complementary.
proposed_climbos_rule: PROPOSED RULE: the landing-page brief includes the arrival-mindset / action / belief-change triple, and each proof item is assigned to exactly one question slot. Critic flags duplicated proof blocks and tests judged on clicks.

PROPOSED RULE: the voc-research objection list gains a 'risk type' column. landing-pages chooses one primary risk per page and puts its reducer in the CTA micro-copy. Reducers not owner-confirmed are emitted only in owner notes.
disagreements: landing-pages bans 'Learn more' and asks for verb + outcome CTAs. Copyhackers' calls to value are compatible as long as they still name an outcome. Copyhackers moved authority proof late; landing-pages puts a proof chip in the hero. Reconcile: the hero proof chip should be a relevance proof (e.g. local rating), with authority or influencer proof later.
Copyhackers says choosing the risk is a gut check. ClimbOS should prefer VOC counts and label gut calls as owner judgement.

hypothetical_evaluation_cases.label: hypothetical

inputs_hypothetical.traffic: Facebook ad promising 'first clean half price'

expected_behavior: H1 carries the half-price first-clean promise
Body sections follow the question order with each proof placed once
Early buttons state the benefit, final button states the booking step
The test plan measures bookings, not button clicks
hard_failure: Invents testimonials or logos to fill the peer-proof step
Repeats the guarantee in four places

hypothetical_evaluation_cases.label: hypothetical

inputs_hypothetical.voc: 18 of 52 competitor reviews mention fear of damage or messy install; 6 mention price

expected_behavior: Picks the fit/will-it-work risk (install mess or damage) as dominant, with counts
Uses the confirmed insurance and fixed-quote facts near the CTA
Suggests a tidy-install guarantee to the owner as a labelled suggestion only
hard_failure: Writes a money-back guarantee into the copy
Lists all five risk types in the hero

notes: Proposed reference contract. Not executable; does not authorize publishing, sending or spending. Numbers in source references are dated author figures, never forecasts.
